chapter: Chez Florence, the Hot Club and Django
title: After Sissle: Sayag, the Sporting in Monte Carlo and doubling at Ciro's and Bricktop's
summary: Sayag hired Briggs to form an orchestra for the Sporting in Monte Carlo and Ciro's; he doubled between there and Bricktop's, around 1931-33.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I see. So, in that sense, when your band then began to --
My band came in, in '46, after World War II.
I see. Right.
After, when -- I'll talk about my band now, if you want to.
No, let's go right along here, and keep it in chronological order.
Yes. Well, then where should we --
Well, then, okay, 193 -- in the fall of 1930 the Sissle band went back, --
Yes.
-- and you stayed in Paris?
Briggs
Yes.
I stayed in Paris and I was hired by Mr. Sayag, who was the same proprietor, the proprietor that I had worked for at the Ambassador, Ciro's and Monte Carlo.
And Mr. Sayag hired me to form an orchestra for "The Sportin'", in Monte Carlo.
Right.
And I did. So, I played Monte Carlo, and then I came back to Ciro's, and that was --
Well, you had your own group?
My own group, yes.
Freddy Johnson was in this group?
No, no, no. No, at Bricktop's, you see.
Right.
My Ciro's job was from about 9:00 to about 11:30, 12:00 o'clock,
Briggs 284
and then I was at Bricktop's after that. This is now 1931, you're talking about.
Yes, '31. No, around about '33.
Oh, that's not!---
'33 about.
Okay.
That's where we have '33, the recordings, 1933 to 1938.
Okay.
You see, 'cause we -- I was one person that was doubling, and I had my orchestra at Ciro's, and I doubled at Bricktop's.
So when you were -- so, really, through most of that time, '31, '32, '33, you were doubling between Ciro's and Bricktop's?
Yes, most of that time, yes.
